newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's envoy blasts U.S. bill on HK journalists.
newsitem.headline: China's envoy blasts U.S. bill on HK journalists.

text.p: China's spokesman in Hong Kong attacked as irresponsible a U.S. congressional bill that would grant visas to Hong Kong journalists after Beijing takes over the territory this year.
The criticism came from Zhang Junsheng, deputy director of the Xinhua news agency, Beijing's de facto embassy in Hong Kong. Zhang is China's official spokesman in the colony.

Illinois Republican Rep. John Porter introduced the bill in the House of Representatives on Thursday. The legislation would provide up to 2,000 Hong Kong journalists with visas after the British colony's handover to China.

"I urge a small number of congressmen not to create an issue here," Zhang told reporters. "He should not express opinions on something he doesn't understand or meddle in other countries' affairs," Zhang said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

Despite China's pledge of a high level of autonomy, anxiety runs deep among Hong Kong's 6.4 million people about whether press freedom will survive, especially since Beijing recently announced plans to trim back democracy and civil liberties in the territory after the sovereignty change.
But Zhang said press freedom was guaranteed in Hong Kong's post-colonial constitution.
"The guarantee of press freedom is clearly stipulated in the Basic Law. I believe journalists in Hong Kong are confident and not worried about press freedom," he said.
"There is no need for an American congressman to make irresponsible remarks," he said.

Under Porter's proposal, the visas would be available to journalists of Hong Kong citizenship or Chinese nationality who have worked in the Hong Kong media for at least three years, along with their immediate family.
